title: Investigate & patch TTFT divergence across model variants impacting premium customers
creator: Miguel Torres
description: Several premium customers reported a pronounced first-token latency (TTFT) and reduced tokens/sec for requests routed to quantized model variants (int8/q4) vs. fp16 variants. The divergence appears intermittent and focused on requests that exercise long-context warmups and cross-worker routing. This ticket tracks triage, a short-term mitigation, and a safe rollout for the permanent fix.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use load profile from customer A (burst 200 QPS -> steady 30 QPS) against model family 'redwood-open-7b-variants'
2) Force route to quantized variant (q4_0) via weight override in routing policy or use dedicated pool with variant tagged
3) Send long prefix prompts (~1k tokens) that trigger KV cache warmup and evaluate first-token latency and sustained tokens/sec for 30s windows
4) Observe TTFT spikes and a ~25-40% drop in tokens/sec compared to fp16 variant under same worker allocation
impact_summary: High impact for a small set of premium customers using Dedicated and Private deployments and some Hosted routes. Customer escalations received (Priority support) citing production regressions and SLA breaches for TTFT. Estimated ~3 customers affected directly and broader risk across similar routing configurations. Business risk: SLA penalties and churn if not resolved quickly.
root_cause_hypothesis: A combination of factors: (1) kernel-selector heuristic aging causes stale chosen kernels to be used for quantized variants on warmed workers leading to suboptimal microbatch sizing; (2) per-model variant router weight calculation underestimates warmup cost and routes bursts to workers without KV priming; (3) new batching handshake change (deployed 2026-02-28) increased initial batch sizing for multiplexed streams which amplifies first-token stalls on quantized variants.
mitigation_plan: Short-term (hotfix, <24h): revert multiplex batching handshake change for routes flagged as 'sensitive-warmup' via config toggle; push runtime flag to reduce initial microbatch target for quantized variants (deployed to hosted canaries)
Medium-term (72h): add per-variant prewarm: when routing weight changes >10% create a transient prewarm request path that populates KV cache before taking production traffic

Long-term (2-3 sprints): adjust kernel-selector to incorporate variant-specific warmup penalty metric and add aging TTL for selected kernels; refine routing cost model to include measured warmup latency for each variant and worker type
rollback_criteria: If canary sees >=5% increase in sustained tokens/sec degradation or error rate >0.5% over baseline, revert flag. For full rollout, revert if customer-reported TTFT regressions increase in the first hour post-rollout.
rollout_plan: Canary (5% traffic) in hosted region us-west-2 with two affected premium accounts invited; monitor dashboard for 60 minutes. If canary stable, expand to Dedicated pools with staged policy changes (1 pool -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) over 6 hours. For Private customers, ship configuration diff and optional operator playbook for manual toggle until auto-upgrade is validated.
related_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/462 - adjust routing cost calc for warmup
comments: 2026-03-10 Miguel Torres: Initial triage - reproduced locally with customer trace. Observed mismatch in kernel selection logs where q4_0 workers kept falling back to a generic matmul kernel that has poor cold-cache latency.

2026-03-11 Priya Shah: Deployed flag to hosted-canary to reduce initial microbatch from 8->4 for quantized variants. Canary showed 18% TTFT improvement after 30m. Rolling patch to dedicated canary pools next.
2026-03-11 Joanna Li (SRE): Added alert rule for variant-TTFT-regression (P90>500ms) and a temp synthetic job to prewarm KV on warmup-sensitive routes.

2026-03-12 Customer Success (Aisha Patel): Notified impacted customers of mitigation and requested acceptance testing window tomorrow morning. Customers requested explicit config for private deployments.

2026-03-13 Code review feedback (runtime team): Addressed race in kernel selector cache invalidation; requested additional unit tests for kernel-aging heuristic. Targeting merge by end-of-day 2026-03-13.
